This applies to every Fell at the shaft. Any Fell still at the river door stays in [[04 - The River Door|The River Door]] until they come down, and joins this fight at the start of the next round when they do.

> [!reminder] How this scene works
> This is the night's big fight, and it is won with stone, not by killing.
> - **The goal.** Set the stone needed across the opening, the place where the shaft comes out into the hollow. The number is 2 plus the floor clock when the Fell first reached the bottom, less any loads already waiting there from scene 5.
> - **How stone arrives.** Shrewish diggers at the top hole lower one load down the rope at the end of every round. A Fell at the top hole can lower one more as their Act, with a Bearing roll.
> - **How stone is set.** A Fell at the opening spends their Act setting one waiting load in mortar, with a Creation or Finesse roll. Each Success or Fellmark sets one.
> - **What fights back.** The Grey Mother, the root itself, has no mind and grows toward warmth. It never moves, and its Acts reach anywhere in the hollow. The flat-eyed Felionis guards the root and goes for whoever is setting stone. Weasels come out of the walls toward the lamps the Fell need to work by.
> - **Ways round the fighting.** A Fell can hold the root back for a round with Rootsummons. The Felionis can be turned out of the fight two ways without hurting it, written out below.
> - **How it ends.** Read the three endings under How this fight is won before you start.
>
> Rootsummons rolls are Brand rolls: 1d6 + Rootsummons competency, 0 tonight, against your 1d6 + 0. A Fellmark raises Rootsummons by 1. They are not spells, so the Felionis's Disrupted does not touch them.

> [!readaloud] Opening: The root wakes
> *For every Fell already at the bottom:* The eyes on the root belong to something. It unfolds out of a fold in the grey, long and low, and drops onto the clay between you and the opening, and the whole root behind it shifts. Up the shaft, faint and far away, Shrewish voices are shouting down that the stone is coming.

> [!readaloud] Opening: Coming down
> *For any Fell who arrives later, from the river door:* You come down the last of the ladder into a low, warm hollow that stinks of rot. The others are already fighting. A root as big as a house fills the far side, pushing up toward the hole you just came through, and a stone wall is half built across the bottom of the shaft.

> [!readaloud] The flat-eyed cat
> It's a hunting cat, long and low, plated in bark. The bark has gone grey and soft at the edges, and it sags. Its forelegs are split at the end, two-pronged, and it walks straight up the clay wall on them. Its eyes are perfectly round and perfectly flat, with nothing behind them. It doesn't growl. It takes up its place on the root, between you and the opening.

> [!lorecheck] Lore: The Felionis
> Any Fell who knows the cat.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* A Felionis. Shervinaw's own hunting cat, grown out of the mother roots, the forest's meanest guard. When a Felionis decides to protect something, spells thrown at it go sour and fall apart. A few have come back out of the grey with their eyes gone flat, and the ones that do still guard. They guard the root now. *Then:* This Fell knows spells will go badly near it, and that it might be reached through the root. Their Lore increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* A Felionis, a cat grown out of the roots, that guards what it chooses. This one has chosen the root.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* A cat. A very big, very wrong cat.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You're sure it's a cat that belongs to someone, and that it will know a friendly voice. *Then:* It does not.

**This applies to a Fell with a Felionis.** The two cats see each other. The flat-eyed one stops for a moment with its head on one side. It goes for someone else first, every round it can. That is story, and it changes no number.

> [!readaloud] The Grey Mother
> Now you can see what the root is. The thing filling the far side of the hollow is the growing end of one, as thick as a house and soft and grey all through, pushing up toward the shaft. Small roots peel off it as you watch and feel their way along the clay. The whole hollow smells of rot and warm wet earth.

> [!secret] The Grey Mother
> This is a mother root no map shows, and it was grey before Nib ever broke into it. It has no mind. It grows toward warmth, and the warmest thing in the riverbank is two hundred people. It cannot be talked to, bargained with or frightened.

> [!reminder] How this fight is won
> It ends one of three ways.
> - **Sealed.** When the last load is set, the root is cut off from the shaft. The Grey Mother is sealed and counts as defeated. Any foe still standing goes still where it is, and the fight ends. Read The last stone. Write down: the shaft is sealed.
> - **Held.** If the floor clock is at 4 when the Fell reach the bottom, or reaches 4 during the fight, the shaft can't be sealed. The Fell hold the root instead. They hold it if at least one Fell is still standing at the end of the third round after that, which gives Dobb the time to get every last Shrewish away. Read The last raft. Write down: the shaft was held until the last raft.
> - **Every Fell falls.** Write down: every Fell fell. Skip scene 7 and read the Defeat ending in [[08 - Dawn on the Sallowrun|Dawn on the Sallowrun]].

> [!lorecheck] Creation: Setting a stone
> A Fell at the opening, as their Act, with a load waiting. They may roll Finesse instead, with the same results.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* The stone goes in square and tight, and you slap the mortar flat with your palm. It's the best course in the wall. *Then:* One load set. Their Creation increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* You heave it into place and press the mortar in round it. It holds. *Then:* One load set.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* It goes in crooked and you have to pull it back out. *Then:* The load is still waiting.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* The stone slips out of your hands and lands on its edge in the clay with a crack. It's still good, but the whole hollow heard it. *Then:* The load is still waiting. This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!lorecheck] Bearing: Lowering a load
> A Fell at the top hole, as their Act.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You feed two stones down the rope one after the other, fast and smooth. *Then:* Two more loads wait at the bottom. Their Bearing increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The rope bites into your hands, and the stone goes down and lands. *Then:* One more load waits at the bottom.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* The stone catches on the bend. You haul it back up. *Then:* No extra load this round.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* The rope slips and the stone goes down the shaft on its own. A long crunch comes up from the bottom. *Then:* No load. This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!lorecheck] Rootsummons: Holding the root
> A Fell with their hands on the root or the clay, as their Act. This is a Brand roll.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You call the living wood and it answers. Clean roots, live ones, crawl out of the clay and wrap round the grey and pull it back. The whole root shudders and stops. *Then:* The Grey Mother takes no Act and no React next round. Their Rootsummons increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The clay answers you. Live roots close round the grey and hold it for a moment. *Then:* The Grey Mother takes no Act next round.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You feel it down there, huge and slow. It doesn't notice you.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You reach too far and the root reaches back. The whole hollow shudders. *Then:* This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!reminder] Getting past the cat without a fight
> The Felionis is a guard, not a hunter. It goes for whoever is setting stone because the stone threatens what it guards. It can be turned out of the fight two ways. A turned Felionis counts as defeated and pays its Lore Points.
> - **Reach the guard under the grey.** A Fell with their hands on the root calls through it with Rootsummons, as their Act.
> - **A Felionis of their own.** A Fell with a Felionis sets their cat between the two, with a Presence roll, as their Act.

> [!lorecheck] Rootsummons: The guard under the grey
> The Fell who reaches through the root, as their Act. This is a Brand roll.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You push your hands into the soft grey and reach. Under the rot is something warm and old and very tired, a cat that was told to guard the shoots and never told to stop. You tell it the root is not a shoot. Its flat eyes flicker. It climbs down off the root, lies down in the clay by the far wall, and does not get up again. *Then:* The Felionis leaves the fight. Their Rootsummons increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The cat stops halfway down the root and stays there, head on one side, watching you and not moving. *Then:* The Felionis leaves the fight.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You reach and there's nothing there but rot. *Then:* The Felionis keeps fighting. Another Fell may try.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You reach too far, and the root reaches back. The whole hollow shudders. *Then:* This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!lorecheck] Presence: Cat to cat
> A Fell with a Felionis of their own, as their Act.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* Your cat walks out across the clay and sits down in front of the grey one, close enough to touch noses. The flat-eyed cat looks at it for a long time. Then it turns and climbs away up the far wall and does not come down. *Then:* The Felionis leaves the fight. Their Presence increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The two cats face each other, and the grey one backs off along the root and stays there. *Then:* The Felionis leaves the fight.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* The flat-eyed cat steps around yours and keeps coming. *Then:* The Felionis keeps fighting. Another Fell may try.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* Your cat goes for it. The two of them go rolling across the clay, spitting, and come apart with nothing settled. *Then:* This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!crucible] The Grey Mother
> [[The Grey Mother]], Champion, a Fell and a half, fights as the floor and walls of the hollow with 11 Vitality. [[The Flat-Eyed Felionis]], Elite, worth one Fell, 7 Vitality, guards the opening and goes for whoever is setting stone. [[Rootbound Weasel]]s, Minions worth half a Fell each, one for every two Fell, 4 Vitality each, come out of the walls toward the lamps. If the Fell got past the weasels in scene 5, these are the same weasels, back for the light. Your Disruption pool is the number of Fell + 1. Spend it only to make the Felionis harder, as Building Crucibles sets out, and only if the Fell are winning easily. The Grey Mother has company, so do not add Vitality to it.

> [!reminder] Nib in this fight
> If Nib is at the bottom, she is not in the fight. She mixes mortar by the opening and hands it to whoever is setting stone. No foe targets her, she cannot fall, and nothing she does triggers a React.

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *When the first load is set:* "That's one. That's one! Keep that cat off us."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *When the cat comes past her:* "Go on, get off, it's not your wall, you horrible thing."

## Sealed

This applies if the last load was set.

> [!readaloud] The last stone
> The last stone goes in. Mortar squeezes out between the joints, and someone slaps it flat with their bare hand. On the other side of the wall the root pushes, and the stones creak, and the wall holds. The small roots feeling along the clay go still, all at once. The cat on the root stops where it is, one foot raised, and doesn't put it down. Up the shaft, far away, the warren stops humming.

## Held

This applies if the Fell held the root for three rounds after the clock reached 4.

> [!readaloud] The last raft
> Up the shaft, faint and far away, you hear Dobb shouting a count. Then a long cheer, and then nothing but the river. They're away. The root stops pushing at the shaft. It turns, slow and huge, toward the warren above, toward the empty hall. Your way back up the shaft is still open, for now.

## Closing the fight

This applies to every Fell who was in the fight.

> [!reminder] Closing the battle
> Close the fight in this order. Name every foe the Fell defeated: the Grey Mother if they sealed the shaft, the Felionis if it fell or was turned, and the weasels if they fell. Then the Fatigue check: you roll 1d6 + 0 once for the table, and each Fell rolls 1d6 + Endurance against it. Then the [[Treasure Phase]]: every Fell who rolled a Fellmark or was granted Luck since their last rest or the end of their last battle takes a Treasure Roll. Lore Points come last, each rating counted once: weasels 1, the Felionis 2, the Grey Mother 3. A seal pays 6 and a hold pays 3.

> [!readaloud] Closing: Going up, if the shaft is sealed
> You climb out of the shaft the way you came, slow, filthy and shaking. The lower tunnels are empty. The cracks in the floor have stopped moving. Upstairs, through the arch at the end of the hall, the sky over the river is starting to go grey.

> [!readaloud] Closing: Going up, if the root was held
> You climb out of the shaft as fast as you can. Behind you, below you, the root is moving again, slow and steady, and the cracks in the lower tunnels are opening wider while you watch. The great hall is empty. Through the river arch, one raft is still at the steps, and Dobb is waving at you to hurry.

> [!beat] Where everyone is now
> Every Fell from the shaft comes up. Any Fell from the river door meets them in the great hall if the shaft is sealed, or on the quay if the root was held. Go to [[07 - Nib's Secret|Nib's Secret]].
